sources.entry: RescueTime - Track time usage and get productivity reports.

summary.name: RescueTime
summary.one_liner: RescueTime is an automatic time tracking app with two parts: RescueTime Focus for app and website tracking, focus sessions and distraction blocking, and RescueTime Timesheets for logging time by client, project, or task.
use_cases: Track how much time goes to apps and websites
Block distracting sites during work sessions
Log billable hours by client or project
Generate invoices and client reports from tracked time
Balance team workloads and see project bottlenecks
Find the most productive hours of the day
summary.what_it_does: RescueTime runs in the background and automatically records time spent on apps and websites. Its Focus part lets users set goals, create alerts, and run focus sessions that block distracting websites, apps, email or chat. Reports show work categories and habit patterns, and real-time insights can help adjust schedules around the most productive hours. Its Timesheets part logs time automatically by project, client, and task, without timers or manual entry, and supports filtering reports for invoices, calendar views, and offline work entry. The page also describes team plans where managers see key tools, productivity trends, and project-level reports.
notable: Two tools in one app: Focus for personal productivity and Timesheets for client and project billing
Automatic tracking of apps and websites with work category reports
Team plans with shared reports, calendars and timelines
Listed in awesome-mac and awesome-ai-tools lists
caveats: Page offers a free 14-day trial; ongoing pricing is not stated on the page
Platforms beyond the web are not named in the page text
Timesheets and team features are described as separate offerings; their cost is not given
